key_insight: Finite element simulations indicate that thermally stressed NiTi-based bilayer hinges can drive prescribed origami folding at reduced unit-cell dimensions.
engineering_relevance: Self-folding thin-film structures could enable compact delivery and controlled deployment of minimally invasive neurovascular implants.
method: Model thermal-expansion mismatch in NiTi–molybdenum and NiTi–SS316L bilayers.
Optimize hinge length, layer thickness, width, and shape using finite element simulations.
Integrate hinges into a waterbomb origami unit cell to evaluate coordinated folding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a simulated hinge design enabling approximately 50% smaller unit-cell dimensions than prior designs and coordinated self-folding in a complete waterbomb unit cell.
watch_item: Simulation results still require experimental validation of microscale fabrication, reliable deployment, and safe thermal actuation in biological environments.
paper_title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
